title: Cheap for a reason
summary: A low P/E can be a bargain — or a business the market expects to shrink. How to tell them apart.

cards.headline: Cheap for a reason
cards.body: A low P/E can mean a bargain, or a business the market expects to shrink. The price is low relative to earnings because those earnings may be falling. A low multiple is a question, not an answer: why is it cheap?

cards.headline: The value trap
cards.body: A value trap looks cheap and stays cheap because the business keeps deteriorating. The multiple never re-rates. The point isn't to avoid low P/Es; it's to ask what that low number is saying about the years ahead.

cards.title: The takeaway
cards.summary: A low P/E is a question about the future, not proof of a bargain.
bullets: Low P/E can mean falling expected earnings.
A value trap stays cheap for a reason.
Ask why it's cheap before calling it cheap.
